comment: UI commands that touch the OS (the clipboard, the page's developer tools) and not the project document, so they have no CLI, MCP or RPC twin (ADR-0026, research 09 section 5.3). Each goes through an allowlisted, validated IPC channel; the walk test in menus.test.ts fails when a host command is missing here or an entry here is no host command.

exempt.reason: Cut in a text field runs main's `edit:run` (enum cut/copy/paste/selectAll) on the focused element. It edits the field's text, never the project, so an agent has nothing to call.
Copy in a text field runs main's `edit:run` on the focused element and writes the OS clipboard. It is the person's clipboard, not project state.
Paste in a text field runs main's `edit:run` on the focused element, reading the OS clipboard. It types into the field the person is in; an agent edits the project through commands.
Select all in a text field runs main's `edit:run` on the focused element. It changes the field's selection, which is page state, not project state.

Copy path, Copy timecode, Copy value, Copy setting key, Copy message and Copy diagnostics put a line of text on the OS clipboard through the renderer. It is the person's clipboard, not project state; an agent reads the same facts from the project, so it has nothing to call.

Reveal in Explorer, Finder or the file manager shows a media file in the OS file manager through `shell:showItemInFolder`, which main validates. It changes nothing in the project, and an agent has no screen to show a folder on.
Open logs folder shows the app's own logs folder in the OS file manager through `shell:openAppFolder`, which main allowlists (settings or logs). It has no project effect and no agent twin.

Import… opens the OS file picker (`dialog:pickMediaFiles`) and then sends the chosen paths as one `media.import`, the command the CLI and MCP call with paths of their own. Only the picker is host; the document change is the catalog command.
Copy command id in the command palette's row menu writes the command's id (`clip.split`) to the OS clipboard through the page's clipboard API. It is the person's clipboard, not project state.
Copy command id in the shortcut editor's row menu writes the command's id (`clip.split`) to the OS clipboard through the page's clipboard API. It is the person's clipboard, not project state.

Opens the page's developer tools at a point (Shift+right-click on dead space) through `window:inspectElement`, which main refuses in packaged builds. A contributor's debugging aid with no project effect.
